payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Given the inventory and nested boundary map, does independent inspection establish completed stuffing, affirmative incompleteness, or unresolved completion, and what requested progress is actually established?
node.criteria: Pass only when established paper-and-cup identity and concrete entry, containment, or compression establish completed stuffing; some paper may remain outside. Fail when affirmative geometry establishes incomplete insertion, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether this failure accompanies positive requested insertion progress or established no progress. Unknown when completion requires an unresolved spatial relation or receiver identity, or when established entry cannot be distinguished as intermediate versus completed stuffing. A boundary-mapping pass is not positive entry evidence. Unresolved source correspondence alone does not invalidate established spatial evidence, but an unresolved edited receiver identity prevents claiming insertion into a cup.
node.binding: Consume s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order as context, then inspect the edited image independently. Read the nested check's typed identity, geometry, progress, and completion findings rather than treating its execution status as their truth value. Revisit specifically localized hidden paper segments and test whether visible containment, compression, or boundary continuity settles stuffing extent. Resolve conflicts only with explicit visible evidence. Do not promote a mapping pass to entry, an entry finding to completion, or completion failure to no progress. Preserve genuine hidden-entry uncertainty; do not infer missing visual facts from the instruction, source cup, hand grip, or altered printing.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible at left, beside a blue cylindrical cup lying on its side; the cup’s oval rim/opening and enclosing wall are clearly visible. Edited: a blue printed paper/card is held in a hand, with its boundaries visible except where covered by the fingers; a reddish rounded object behind it has a curved outline and a dark curved line, but its boundaries and structure are partly obscured. The edited image does not visibly establish that this object is the source cup: its visible shape differs from the source cup’s rim-and-wall structure, and correspondence is unresolved. The paper and candidate receiving object are both present in the edited image; no insertion is established.

Boundary map: The blue printed paper has a visible upper edge running from the hand-covered area near the upper left toward a pointed corner at upper right; its right edge descends diagonally to a lower-right corner, and its lower edge runs back toward a lower-left point. Fingers obscure portions of the upper-left and left boundaries; the visible endpoints lie around the hand, with no visible paper segment disappearing behind the reddish object. The reddish rounded object is behind the paper: the paper overlaps its left side, while a dark curved line is visible on the exposed right portion. The object’s boundary and structure are partly obscured, and it is not established as a cup; no alternative receiver is evident. Findings: receiver identity unresolved; geometry unresolved (the visible overlap does not establish entry or exclude it at obscured regions); requested progress unresolved; completion unresolved. The map is grounded in visible edges and overlap, but does not establish stuffing into a cup.
